newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tietmeyer says not right time to discuss EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says not right time to discuss EMU delay.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Friday that it was not the right time to discuss any possible delay in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
Tietmeyer, who was speaking after addressing the Danish businessmen's Borsen Executive Club, declined to comment on Germany's ability to meet EMU criteria.
"I hope that Germany will be able to participate...it is not the right time to discuss this, let's wait until spring 1998," he said.
He said that if there proved at that time to be more than one country which qualified for EMU then it would go ahead on time on January 1,1999.
"If Germany does not fulfil the criteria, we have no objection to other countries going ahead," he said.
Tietmeyer, who was speaking in English, added though that he thought it improbable that EMU could start without Germany and France.
On current dollar levels and their possible impact on German inflation, he said:

"I understand that there has already been some rise of import prices. There is no doubt about that but we do not think that this will have a spillover effect on the overall (inflation) situation in Germany."
"We do not think it ... is dangerous," Tietmeyer said.
On interest rates, Tietmeyer said that he did not see higher German interest rates in the coming months.
"We all have our own monetary policies. There is no need in Germany to raise interest rates in the coming months," he said.
